description:
FOUND by the fz-kdt.127.2 adversarial refutation (F5), folded-commit
1d7943335's successor.

src/compiler2/types/types_test.rs::erased_closure_dnf_hygiene::branded_pair
builds its two literals with ZERO captures:

    let left  = t.closure_lit(ClosureTarget(3), vec![], 1);
    let right = t.closure_lit(ClosureTarget(4), vec![], 1);

Under fz-kdt.127.2's erasure a capture-free literal is DROPPED WHOLE (there is
nothing left to say once the brand is gone), so both arms become the bare
arrow before the module's two tests ever look at them. What they now pin is
"two bare arrows intern as one", not the hazard the module exists for.

The hazard the module documents (and .agent/docs/set-theoretic-types.md:126
states) is that `erase_closure_identity` makes two DISTINCT clauses equal IN
PLACE, after union-time dedupe has already run, so only `Types::intern`'s
`dedupe_exact_clauses` can catch the resulting `A OR A` -- and after
fz-kdt.127.2 that case lives exclusively in the capture-BEARING literal:
`erase(L3(int) | L5(int))` is one anonymous clause `closure[?](int)`, reached
from two.

NOT A DEFECT TODAY: the refuter measured the collapse holding --
`erase(L3(int) | L5(int)) == erase(L3(int))` is true, and the 32-site
same-typed int-capture `Enum.find` ladder shares perfectly (59 executables at
base and at head). This is missing COVERAGE.

WORK: give `branded_pair` a capture (or add a capture-bearing twin) so both
`erasing_two_brands_of_one_surface_leaves_one_funcs_clause` and
`the_activation_key_of_an_erased_union_is_the_key_of_each_arm` run on the case
the erasure can actually collapse. Prove it red-first by disabling
`dedupe_exact_clauses` and watching the capture-bearing arm go red where the
zero-capture arm stays green.
title: erased_closure_dnf_hygiene covers only ZERO-capture literals, so the A-or-A hazard in the capture-BEARING case the type-preserving key created is untested
